title: Supported Defence: Take Munich
briefing: Industrial era. You are India with three Riflemen standing next to Munich, a walled German city of size 5, on its west side. India is at War with Germany. A German Rifleman holds Munich and three more German Riflemen stand next to it on the east side. Your home city, Chittor, is six tiles west. This tries a new rule, supported defence: units the defender orders into its own city while you attack it support the city. The walls take the first damage. What gets through is shared between the garrison and every supporter, and each of them strikes back at your attackers. If the garrison falls, the supporter that can take the most damage moves in. The city falls only when the garrison and all its supporters are dead. Pinning a supporter, by attacking it where it stands, stops it supporting that turn. Take Munich within 10 turns. Does supporting a city feel right, and can three attackers still take it?
tests: Does supporting a city feel right, and can three attackers still take it?

objective.summary: Take Munich by turn 11, keeping your own cities.
